test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A train crosses a one km long bridge in one minute and a 750 m long tunnel in 50 seconds. Assuming the train is running at a uniform speed, what is its speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in length = 1000 m − 750 m = 250 m

Difference in time = 60 s − 50 s = 10 s

Speed = 250 ÷ 10 = 25 m/s

Speed in km/h = 25 × 18 ÷ 5 = 90 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 90 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Bridge length** = 1 km = 1000 m, **Time taken** = 1 min = 60 s

**Tunnel length** = 750 m, **Time taken** = 50 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When a train crosses an object with length (bridge/tunnel), Total Distance = **Train Length** + **Object Length**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/874716c7a19f88f45a9959e79f081e788738998c512ad750b134b801d8d94949.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **length of the train** be L.

⇒ Speed = (L + 1000) ÷ 60 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Speed = (L + 750) ÷ 50 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ (L + 1000) ÷ 60 = (L + 750) ÷ 50

⇒ 5 × (L + 1000) = 6 × (L + 750)

⇒ 5L + 5000 = 6L + 4500

⇒ L = 500 m

⇒ Speed = (500 + 1000) ÷ 60 = 1500 ÷ 60 = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/h = 25 × 18 ÷ 5

⇒ Speed = 5 × 18 = 90 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 90 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Train Crossing a Pole or Stationary Point

When a train crosses a pole or a person, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train (L).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction with speeds u and v, the relative speed is |u − v|.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions with speeds u and v, the relative speed is (u + v).</p
